name: Universidad de Salamanca, principal facade
aka: Fachada de la Universidad de Salamanca

dates.note: The Spanish article's first sentence is 'La fachada de la Universidad de Salamanca data de 1529'. The node's exemplar gives 'c. 1512-1529'; the article states only the one year and no start.

refs.title: Fachada de la Universidad de Salamanca - Wikipedia, la enciclopedia libre

survey.prepared: No revision date was printed in the extract. AN ENCYCLOPEDIA ARTICLE AND NOT A REGISTER.

quotes.text: La fachada de la Universidad de Salamanca data de 1529 y pertenece al estilo plateresco, que se desarrolló en los primeros 30 años del siglo XVI. Se caracteriza por una minuciosa y abundante decoración. Para muchos, esta fachada es la obra maestra del plateresco español.

quotes.page: Spanish Wikipedia, section 'Análisis', its first line

quotes.text: En el segundo cuerpo vemos tres escudos: el más grande tiene representaciones de los reinos de la Corona Hispánica con una cruz sobre una corona.

measurements.name: portada_register_count
measurements.note: THE CENTRAL FIGURE OF THIS NODE, STATED BY A SOURCE. The node's own description says the retablo facade is 'three registers of villamayor sandstone against a plain wall'; the article says the facade is divided into three cuerpos. Registers, not storeys: the wall behind carries its own windows on a different rhythm.

note: Tranche 3, 5 Sep 2026. This is the one record in the cluster whose source states the node's own governing number -- three registers -- in its own words. TWO THINGS WERE REMOVED FROM THIS RECORD BEFORE IT WAS COMMITTED AND BOTH ARE WORTH KNOWING. A UNESCO reference for the Old City of Salamanca was drafted from memory of the number and deleted: no UNESCO page was read for it in this session, and a plausible id is exactly the laundered citation this layer exists to prevent. And a `portada_bay_count` measurement was drafted whose `as_printed` was in a paragraph of the article that no quote here carries; the article's analysis names a 'calle central' and a 'calle de la izquierda' and a right, which is three vertical bays, but it never counts them and reading three out of three mentions is an inference. Neither omission is a gap in the source.
